response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.WBC) AS avg_wbc, AVG(L.HGB) / AVG(L.HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM p) SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, p.avg_wbc, p.ratio, p.ratio - m.mean_ratio AS diff FROM p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.ratio > m.mean_ratio ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A patient's HGB/HCT ratio is the ratio of their average HGB to their average HCT (each average ignores NULLs), not the average of per-record ratios.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios, skipping patients whose ratio is NULL. A NULL mean makes the comparison false, so no rows are returned.

alternatives.interpretation: The patient's ratio is the average of the per-record HGB/HCT ratios, using only records where both values are present.
alternatives.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.WBC) AS avg_wbc, AVG(L.HGB * 1.0 / L.HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM p) SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, p.avg_wbc, p.ratio, p.ratio - m.mean_ratio AS diff FROM p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.ratio > m.mean_ratio ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 10
